resources.string: A timer for work and rest intervals, with cues loud enough for the gym.
What stays on this phone, and what %1$s gets
The fonts and libraries Interval is built with
Interval keeps everything on this device. There are no accounts, no analytics and no ads, and nothing leaves the phone unless you send it.

Your workouts, presets, plan, settings, body weight and Lift sessions, in the app's own storage. Export, in Settings, puts the lot in one file for you to keep; Android's backup carries it to a new phone with your other apps' data.
A finished workout, a session or your export goes nowhere until you choose an app to share it with. What that app does with it is up to that app.

If you connect %1$s in Settings, each workout and Lift session you finish is written there as a workout, with its intervals or sets, how hard you said it was and any note you wrote on it, and, when you have set a body weight, its calorie estimate. Interval reads two things from %1$s: your latest body weight, which the weight sheet in Settings offers to use, set only when you tap it; and your heart rate during a workout or session you finished, as a watch recorded it there, whose average and peak its summary and page show. Both stay on this device like the weight you set yourself. Turn it off in Settings, or take the permission back in %1$s, and nothing more is written; what was written stays there for you to keep or delete.
